question: Where must YIELD signs be used at a roundabout, and may they control the circulatory roadway?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A YIELD sign is mandatory at the entrance to a roundabout to require entering road users to yield the right-of-way. YIELD signs must control only the approach roadways — they may not be used to control the circulatory roadway itself. Standards (mandatory): - "A YIELD sign shall be used to require road users to yield the right-of-way to other traffic at the entrance to a roundabout. YIELD signs at roundabouts shall be used to control the approach roadways and shall not be used to control the circulatory roadway." Guidance (recommended): - On an approach to a circular intersection controlled by a YIELD sign and at uncontrolled exits, crosswalks should be a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of the circulatory roadway. Options (permitted): - YIELD (word) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts. - At roundabouts where ONE WAY signs have been installed in the central island, Roundabout Circulation (R6-5P) plaques may be placed below the YIELD signs on approaches to supplement the central island signs. - The Vehicular Traffic Warning sign assembly may be installed on an approach to a circular intersection controlled by a YIELD sign where the crosswalk is at least 20 feet in advance of the yield point at the entrance to the circulatory roadway. - The Non-Vehicular Warning sign assembly may likewise be installed on such an approach where the crosswalk is at least 20 feet in advance of the yield point. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows optional YIELD word markings, yield lines, and crosswalks set back a minimum of 20 feet on the approach roadways to a roundabout, with no yield control within the circulatory roadway. - [Image 2] Shows Section 3D.05, permitting YIELD (word) and YIELD AHEAD pavement markings on approaches to roundabouts. - [Image 3] Shows Section 2B.51, permitting Roundabout Circulation plaques below YIELD signs on approaches to roundabouts. - [Image 4] Shows the Section 2B.10 Standard requiring YIELD signs at roundabout entrances to control approach roadways only, not the circulatory roadway. - [Image 5] Shows Section 3C.09 guidance that crosswalks on YIELD-controlled approaches should be a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of the circulatory roadway. Citations: - Section 2B.10 Standard §5 (p.78) - Section 3C.09 Guidance §3 (p.593) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 2B.51 Option §4 (p.118) - Section 2C.54 Option §11 (p.192) - Section 2C.55 Option §6 (p.193) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596)
gold_answer: A YIELD sign must control each entering approach roadway. It must not be used to control the circulatory roadway.
